/Through Wednesday/...
Issued at 1158 AM MDT Wed Sep 30 2026

GOES satellite imagery shows the well defined, strong trough moving 
east across the AZ/NM border, roughly dead center N-S across 
those two states. The trough and remnants of Polo have fully 
merged and the moist conveyor belt well east of the trough is 
truly impressive, especially if you live in Texas, Oklahoma, and 
Kansas. The best forcing from the trough will remain over New 
Mexico and Oklahoma next 24-36 hours, and the TROWAL/deformation 
zone of precip will impact mostly southern Colorado now through
tonight. Radar shows widely scattered showers across Lincoln 
County and more stratiform rain along the crest of the Palmer
Divide. Over an inch of rain has fallen since early this morning
across far southern Lincoln County. The axis of best lift with 
the deformation zone extends from Lincoln County west along the 
Palmer to northwest Park County, where the moderate rain is 
expected to continue into the late evening hours. There is no 
lightning anywhere in the state as of midday, though there should 
be some instability available this afternoon for a 10-20% chance 
of a thunderstorm across that same area along the southern edge of
our CWA. Another inch, maybe 1.5" could fall across Lincoln 
County through early Thursday morning, and across the Palmer 
Divide to northwest Park County perhaps an inch total through 
Thursday morning. The surface low currently is across the OK/TX 
panhandles and weak pressure falls indicate it will move into 
central KS after midnight. The southern track of the 500 mb 
trough, and a 1004 mb surface low over the panhandles both meant 
rainfall amounts would be limited across our area other than 
Lincoln County. There is high confidence in the rainfall shutting 
off entirely Thursday morning. Further north and west this
afternoon/evening, light rain is about all to expect along and 
north of I-70 this afternoon and evening. North of I-76 and north 
of CO-66 (more or less), probably no precip will occur. In terms 
of mountain precipitation the rest of today into tomorrow, the 
Park/Gore Ranges and the Front Range from RMNP northward are not 
expected to see much if any accumulating rain or snow. The 
Mosquito/Tenmile range and southern Front Range from JeffCo into 
Park County should see several tenths of rain, and T-3" of snow 
above 11,500 ft elevation. No travel impacts are expected. In 
terms of temperatures, extensive cloud cover in the comma head of
the trough means temperatures will not get out of the 60s south 
of I-76, but should reach about 70 across the norther tier 
counties. Where it's raining, temps should be in the 50s to low 
60s. Thursday will see more sun, especially north and west of 
Lincoln County, with temps across the plains warming to the low 
70s, with 60s across the Palmer Divide and Lincoln County, and the
mountain valleys. South Park, with early morning rain showers and
some lingering cloud cover may remain in the 50s on Thursday.

The ridge builds over Colorado Friday through Sunday, and our entire 
area looks to be dry with above normal temperatures trending well 
above normal by the weekend. With the ridge overhead, winds will not 
be an issue and thus we also don't expected any fire weather 
issues. Highs on Friday should be upper 70s to around 80 across 
the plains, and 60s to lower 70s in the mountain valleys. On 
Saturday, add 3-5 degrees across the board. Sunday and Friday will
be similar temperature wise as the thermal ridge at 700 mb slides
east of Colorado, cooling afternoon highs 3-5 degrees.

Next week looks dry across the plains, but there is quite a bit of 
uncertainty in the Monday afternoon through Tuesday timeframe.  The 
deterministic models show a weak short wave trough moving across 
Colorado. Some sub-tropical moisture might make it northeast into
Colorado associated with the trough. At a minimum we have 15-30% 
PoP across the high country, where available ensemble model output
indeed has increasing chances of rain, but even the 90th 
percentile amounts are 0.1-0.2" this far out. It also looks far 
too warm to snow below 12,000 ft. A handful of ensemble members 
from each modeling system have any measurable precip for the I-25 
urban corridor, and even fewer for the northeast plains. Well 
above normal temperatures should continue across our area next 
week with low 80s across the plains (perhaps even mid 80s, yikes) 
and 60s in the mountain valleys and eastern foothills.
